Ishita: hey, did you post the "wheat shortage" message in the building group?
Aditi: yes! my cousin forwarded it, said shops will run out by tonight 😰
Ishita: it's fake, the food office says stocks are normal. Everyone's rushing to the stores
Aditi: oh no. I also wrote that Gupta Stores is hiding stock
Ishita: yeah, Mr Gupta's shop was mobbed and he's upset
Aditi: I feel sick. Deleting it now.
Aditi: Posted in the group: "Correction: my earlier message was false. Stocks are normal. Sorry for the panic."
Aditi: I'm going to his shop to apologise in person
Ishita: good. Maybe check before forwarding next time?
Aditi: from now on I check first, forward second 🙂

qa.q: What did Aditi's message say about Gupta Stores?
qa.a: It said Gupta Stores is hiding stock.

qa.q: How was Aditi feeling when Ishita said Mr Gupta's shop had been mobbed?
qa.a: Aditi felt sick and guilty, and moved straight to delete the message.

qa.q: What did Aditi do to repair the harm, and what would help in future?
qa.a: Aditi deleted the message, posted a correction in the same group and went to apologise in person. Checking before forwarding would help in future.

qa.q: How might Mr Gupta have experienced the false message?
qa.a: He was upset, since a crowd mobbed his shop because of a rumour naming it. An apology face to face may help him feel the record is straight.

grounding: Sharing a false message causes panic and hurts someone named; delete, correct to the same audience, apologise, and check before sharing.

passage:
Tanvir's diary, Friday, very late

I made a mess today and I need to write it out.

This morning I shared a message in our colony group: a child kidnapper had been seen near the school, a vegetable vendor with a blue cart. I didn't check. I was scared for my niece.

By noon, parents had surrounded Ujjwal-bhaiya, the man who sells vegetables from a blue cart, shouting. Someone pushed him. The police came and said there was no such report anywhere. The message was months old, from another state.

I felt sick. I deleted my post. Then I wrote a correction in the same group, in capitals: FALSE. MY MISTAKE. PLEASE DON'T FORWARD.

In the evening I went to Ujjwal-bhaiya's cart. I said sorry, by name, in front of the neighbours. He was quiet, then said, "Just check next time."

I will. Shame isn't enough. I need the habit.

qa.q: What did the false message say about the kidnapper?
qa.a: That a vegetable vendor with a blue cart had been seen near the school.

qa.q: What did Tanvir feel after the police said there was no such report?
qa.a: Tanvir felt sick with guilt and shame for sharing a false message that led to Ujjwal-bhaiya being pushed.

qa.q: What steps did Tanvir take to repair the harm?
qa.a: Tanvir deleted the post, posted a clear correction to the same group, and apologised to Ujjwal-bhaiya by name in front of the neighbours.

qa.q: How might Ujjwal-bhaiya see the apology?
qa.a: Ujjwal-bhaiya may feel hurt but somewhat respected, accepting it quietly while asking Tanvir to check next time.

grounding: The diary shows someone who shared something false that caused panic and hurt a named person, deleting it, correcting it to the same audience and apologising, and committing to check first.

passage:
Shalini: Vandana, did you post that my pharmacy sells fake medicines?
Vandana: I shared a message from the society group
Vandana: it said the chemist near gate 2 was caught
Shalini: That's me. Nobody caught anyone. My phone hasn't stopped ringing. Two regular customers cancelled orders.
Vandana: oh no
Vandana: I'm checking now
Vandana: the message is about a shop in a different city. from last year
Vandana: Shalini I'm so sorry
Shalini: Please fix it. Where you posted it.
Vandana: deleting now. posting a correction in the society group and my status
Vandana: "I shared a false message about the pharmacy near gate 2. It was about a different city. The pharmacy is not involved. Sorry to Shalini."
Shalini: Thank you
Vandana: from now on I'm checking before I forward anything. I mean it
Shalini: ok. That helps

qa.q: How many regular customers cancelled orders?
What was Vandana feeling on realising the message was false?
qa.a: Vandana felt shocked and guilty, apologising at once for hurting Shalini's business.

qa.q: Why was posting the correction in the same places important?
qa.a: Because the same people who saw the false message needed to see the correction, which is what repairs the harm.

qa.q: How does Shalini see Vandana's correction?
qa.a: Shalini is still upset but feels it helps, thanking Vandana once the correction is posted where the rumour spread.

grounding: The chat shows someone who shared something false that hurt a named person, deleting it, posting a correction to the same audience, apologising and committing to check first.
